summary: A. V. Williams Jackson specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He studied at Columbia University and Halle-Wittenberg under Edward Delavan Perry and Edward Washburn Hopkins. He later served as fellow and professor at Columbia (1883–1935).

Aaron P. Proffitt works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned degrees from the University of Colorado and the University of Michigan, studying under Micah L. Auerback, Donald S. Lopez, Jr., and others, before joining SUNY Albany around 2015.

Abanindranath Tagore was an Indian scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College and University, and the Government College of Art & Craft, later holding a post at the University of Calcutta (~1921–1929).

Abdur Rehman is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and also studied under Ahmad Hasan Dani, later teaching archaeology at the University of Peshawar (attested 1988).

Abel Bergaigne was a French scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault. He held posts as répétiteur at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1888) and lecturer at the Sorbonne and University of Paris.

Abhiraj Rajendra Mishra is an Indologist who studied under traditional teacher Rambhadracharya. He has served as head of the Sanskrit department at Himachal Pradesh University, visiting professor at the University of Indonesia, and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Abigail I. MacBain works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at McMaster University (attested 2008), where she studied under teachers including James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, Mark MacWilliams, Mark Rowe, and Michael Greenwald.

Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron was a French scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at the Sorbonne, Amersfoort, and under Darab Kumana, holding posts at the Bibliothèque nationale and Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres.

Abraham Sachs was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at Johns Hopkins University. He held an appointment at the Institute for Advanced Study in 1945 and served on the faculty at Brown University from around 1948 to 1983.

Abraham Yohannan was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as religious studies. He studied at Columbia University and later held an academic post there from approximately 1894 to 1925.
Abraham Zablocki is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University and held an academic post at Agnes Scott College (attested 2008).
Acharya Buddharakkhita studied under U Nārada and Mahasi Sayadaw, and he later taught Laurence Khantipalo Mills.

Achim Bayer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg, studying under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, and worked as a research associate at the University of Munich (2004–2006).

Achyutananda Dash is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He was a Commonwealth Visiting Fellow at the University of Oxford (1997–1998) and held a post at Dr. Hari Singh Gour University (attested 1999).

Adalbert Bezzenberger was a German linguist and Indologist who studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and at Munich. He taught at Göttingen before becoming professor of Sanskrit, prorector, and rector at the University of Königsberg between 1879 and 1921.

Adalbert Kuhn was a German linguist and Indologist who studied under Franz Bopp at the University of Berlin (1833–1837). He served as teacher, professor, and director at the Köllnisches Gymnasium between 1837 and 1870.

Adam Bowles specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at La Trobe University under Greg Bailey in 2004 and later served as a senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland (attested 2016–2018).

Adam Hardy is an architectural historian working in Indology and archaeology. He studied architecture at the University of Cambridge and held professorships at De Montfort University (~1993–2004) and Cardiff University (~2004), also directing PRASADA.

Adam Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under supervisors Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, while also studying under numerous traditional Tibetan teachers.

Adele Schlombs is a scholar in sinology, history, and archaeology. She held posts at the Museum of East-Asian Art in 1991 and at the Museum für Ostasiatische Kunst Köln from approximately 1991 to 2022.
